title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a notational preamble for the 'de Rham complex with divided powers' notes. Earlier pages set up, for an abelian category A, four variants of an object K: K^* (cosemi-simplicial), K_* (semi-simplicial), K^· (cochain complex) and K_· (chain complex). They are linked by Dold–Kan/Dold–Puppe type equivalences DP and ND (normalisation), and by duality.

The page makes four points.

1. An object of (A_*)^·, a cochain complex in the category A_* of semi-simplicial objects of A, can be read the other way round. Via the canonical equivalence σ: (A_*)^· ≅ (A^·)_*, which simply exchanges the order of the two indexings, it is a (semi-)simplicial object in the category A^· of cochain complexes, n ↦ K^·_{[n]}.

2. The other mixed categories are read in the same way: A_{*·}, A_{·*}, A^{*·}, A^*_·, A^·_*, and so on.

3. Objects of (A^·)^· are cochain bicomplexes and objects of (A_·)_· are chain bicomplexes. Objects of (A_·)^· or (A^·)_· are mixed chain–cochain bicomplexes: chains in one index, cochains in the other. For K^{··} and K_{··} the associated total ('simple') complex is a cochain or chain complex respectively. In the mixed case the total complex a priori has terms in both positive and negative degrees.

4. Grothendieck notes that a degree convention would have to be fixed: total degree i−j or j−i, depending on whether cochains or chains are given preference. The next page adds that he has not yet seen an urgent need for such a convention.

The purpose is bookkeeping. The conventions are needed to handle divided-power de Rham complexes, which combine simplicial and cosimplicial structures through Dold–Kan, together with their duals.
errors: No mathematical errors. The equivalence σ is just the swap of indexing, (A_*)^· = Fun(semi-simplicial index × cochain index, A) read in either order, so it is trivially correct. The degree convention for mixed bicomplexes is explicitly left open.

ideas.what: Exchange equivalence (A_*)^· ≅ (A^·)_*: a complex of semi-simplicial objects equals a semi-simplicial object in complexes
ideas.modern_name: Currying / interchange of diagram categories (Fun(I,Fun(J,A)) ≅ Fun(J,Fun(I,A)))

ideas.what: Cochain, chain and mixed chain–cochain bicomplexes, with total complexes; the mixed case gives total degrees of both signs, so a sign/degree convention is needed
ideas.modern_name: Bicomplexes and totalization (e.g. Tot of a double complex in the second quadrant, homological vs cohomological grading)

deep.surprise_reason: Purely notational housekeeping (mixed index categories, bicomplexes, total degree conventions). It is standard material, only interesting as context for the divided-power de Rham / Dold–Puppe project.
transcription_corrections: 'un objet simplicial dans la catégorie A^·' should likely read 'un objet ½ simplicial dans la catégorie A^·' (semi-simplicial, consistent with A_* on the previous page).

The final unclear lines likely read roughly: 'si par le degré total l'objet d'indices i et j est en degré i−j ou j−i, suivant qu'on donne la préférence aux cochaînes ou aux chaînes', which continues onto the next page.
The page number '310' at the bottom is the archive folio number, not mathematical content.
